judged_text: The booking row is updated with createMany of attendees but the new attendee emails are never pushed to the existing calendar event attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and guests already present on the booking's calendar entry are not reconciled with the evt attendee list ordering. Depending on EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees semantics, the calendar event can be rebuilt with an attendee list that includes the just-created DB rows, so any failure between the Prisma update and the calendar update leaves the database and the external calendar event permanently out of sync (attendees on the booking but not invited on the calendar event), with no rollback of the created Attendee rows.

Depending on EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees semantics, the calendar event can be rebuilt with an attendee list that includes the just-created DB rows, so any failure between the Prisma update and the calendar update leaves the database and the external calendar event permanently out of sync (attendees on the booking but not invited on the calendar event), with no rollback of the created Attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, and only afterwards `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating logic if the calendar update throws/fails, so the booking can end up with new attendee rows in the database that were never applied to the external calendar. (The finding’s claim that new guests are “never pushed” to `evt.attendees` is incorrect—`evt.attendees` is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees`, which includes the newly created rows—but the out-of-sync/rollback issue is directly supported by the diff.)
